title: Every consumer of a hub event spells out all 76 event kinds; 1,008 lines of no-op match arms in this slice
reason: The counts hold. `grep -cE '^\s*\| EventKind::'` gives app 282, turn 213, window 152, pages 143, offer 74, context_view 72 (not 73) and approvals 71, which is 1,007 lines. The lints are set to deny in Cargo.toml:73-74. approvals.rs:31 has the 5-element KINDS array and the match at :429. is_block (app.rs:2869) decides on two kinds. docs/code-quality/lints.md:70-80 backs the `matches!`/`==` route: it says a match that handles one variant and ignores the rest should use `if let` or `matches!`, and that the lints are for matches that must grow with the enum. The claim is overstated in one place. Each new classification function is itself an exhaustive match over all 76 kinds, about 76 lines each, so five or six concerns add roughly 400-450 lines back. The net saving is therefore well under 650. Removing the lists outright with `matches!` saves the most, but it gives up the 'a new kind forces a decision' property for those functions.
evidence: `EventKind` (crates/contract/src/events.rs:82) has 76 named kinds plus `Unknown`. Because wildcard arms are denied, each function that cares about a few kinds lists all the others as `| EventKind::X` lines ending in `=> {}` or `=> false`. I counted bare `| EventKind::X` continuation lines per product file: app.rs 282, turn.rs 213, window.rs 152, pages.rs 143, offer.rs 74, context_view.rs 73, approvals.rs 71, which is 1,008 lines in this slice across 14 lists (app.rs 4, turn.rs 3, window.rs 2, pages.rs 2, one each in the other three). Across the whole tui crate the same count is 2,091 lines in 29 lists. Example: `is_block` (app.rs:2869-2970) decides on 2 kinds and spends about 78 lines naming the rest. approvals.rs states its interest twice: a 5-element `KINDS` array at line 31, then a match at line 429 that handles those 5 and lists the other 71. The same pattern exists for the `Waiting` enum (the tag on a command awaiting its answer): `Waiting::ArchiveDiscovery` appears in 11 exhaustive lists in product code, 3 of them in app.rs (1796, 1916, 2237).
prop: Keep the rule's goal (a new kind forces a decision) but pay for it once per concern instead of once per function. Add small classification functions next to `EventKind` in `contract` (or one tui module), each a single exhaustive match that maps a kind to a narrow enum or `Option`, for example `EventKind::approval() -> Option<ApprovalKind>` with the 5 kinds approvals.rs folds, and similar for turn-shaping kinds, usage/context kinds and command answers. Consumers then match the narrow enum exhaustively. A new event kind is still a compile error, but in a handful of classification functions rather than 29 lists. For functions that test one or two kinds (`is_block`), an `if kind == ...` chain or `matches!` already compiles today (app.rs uses `envelope.kind() == EventKind::CommandAccepted` at line 2307) and removes the list outright.

title: `App::on_session` contains two identical 100-line blocks for answers from a session that is not on screen
reason: I diffed app.rs:2343-2442 against 2453-2555 with whitespace ignored. The only difference is a three-line comment ('No `commands_answered`...'). The delegate branch also calls `fold_delegate` just before its match (around line 2340). That call sits outside the shared block and would stay where it is, so a shared helper works as proposed.
evidence: `on_session` runs from app.rs:2202 to 2812 (611 lines). Inside it, the branch for the open delegate's session (lines 2343-2442) and the branch for any other non-attached session (lines 2453-2555) each match on the event kind, handle `CommandAccepted` (settle, then a possible workspace-change follow-up) and `CommandRejected` (workspace-change refusal, then `refused`), and list every other kind as a no-op. A whitespace-insensitive diff of the two ranges shows they differ only by a three-line comment and a trailing `return send;`. Each block is 100 lines, about 75 of which are the no-op kind list.
prop: Extract one private method, for example `settle_foreign_answer(&mut self, envelope, move_from, waiting, send)`, and call it from both branches. That removes 100 lines and one of the four exhaustive kind lists in app.rs, and it gives `on_session` its first real seam: the remaining function is then the attached-session fold, which could move to its own file with the three session cases (open item, other session, attached) as separate methods.

title: A 1,223-line recording test fake is compiled into the product as the default configuration seam
reason: lib.rs:22 declares `mod configure_fake;` with no `#[cfg(test)]`. config_views.rs:162 defaults to `Arc::new(Fake::new(Vec::new()))`. `impl Configure for Fake` runs from 615 to 1196 and is not cfg(test), and the struct plus FakeLogin take lines 1-358. Only 362-550, the row helpers and the tests module are test-only, so about 940 product lines is right. A product path where the fake really stays in place does exist. `remote::seams` returns `seam: None` (remote.rs:1083), and `Launch.configure` defaults to `None` (crates/main/src/launch.rs:133). Because of that, the `Option` plus the UNAVAILABLE message (config_views.rs:35) is the variant of the proposal that works, not a mandatory seam in `App::new`.
evidence: configure_fake.rs opens with "A recording `Configure` for the views' tests" and holds `Fake`, a struct of several dozen `Mutex` fields that record every read and write, plus `FakeLogin` and gates for holding installs. It is declared in lib.rs:22 as a plain `mod configure_fake;` with no `#[cfg(test)]`, because `ConfigViews::default()` (app/config_views.rs:162) builds `Arc::new(Fake::new(Vec::new()))` as a placeholder until the loop calls `set_configure` or `set_remote` (event_loop.rs:268-270). `Configure` is the trait through which the views read and write configuration; it has three implementations (the real one in crates/main/src/configure.rs:266, `Remote` in remote.rs:648, and this fake). About 950 of the file's lines sit outside `#[cfg(test)]` blocks, and since `Fake` is reachable as a `dyn Configure`, all 30 of its trait methods are kept in the release binary. If a product path ever reached a view before the real seam was set, the person would see an empty settings list that silently records writes to memory instead of an error.
prop: Make the absence of a seam explicit instead of standing a fake in for it: either pass the seam to `App::new` (the loop already has it before the first frame) or hold `Option<Arc<dyn Configure>>` and have the views say "nothing to address" when it is `None` (config_views.rs already has a constant for that message at line 35). Then declare `#[cfg(test)] mod configure_fake;`. The jigs in jigs.rs build `App::new(None)` and never open a configuration view, so they need no seam. No repository lines are deleted, but about 950 lines leave the product build.

title: `App` is driven through 39 `*_inner` functions that leave settling to the caller, with 23 test-only wrappers that settle for the tests
reason: The counts hold: 39 `*_inner` functions, 25 (not 26) carrying the 'Handles the route without settling' doc line, and 23 `#[cfg(test)]` wrappers whose names match an inner (I computed this with comm). The proposal as written would change behaviour. `handle_events_inner` (event_loop.rs:771-) runs a whole batch of terminal events, including key, edit, mouse and quota sends, through the inner forms, and `settle_and_send` (740-745) then settles once per batch. An `apply` that settles once per input would settle once per event in the batch. The single entry would have to take the batch, or keep a non-settling form, so some of the split stays. Most of the wrappers are short, so the saving is closer to 40 lines than 70.
evidence: "Settling" is the layout pass that re-clamps scroll and trims pages after state changes (`App::settle`). The tui crate has 39 product functions named `*_inner`; 26 carry the doc line "Handles the route without settling; the caller owns the layout pass". The event loop calls only the `_inner` forms (event_loop.rs:1009-1125 calls `on_line_inner`, `connect_failed_inner`, `write_failed_inner`, `on_files_inner`, `on_models_inner`, `on_image_inner`, `on_feedback_inner`, `set_size_inner`, `load_inner`, `load_failed_inner`, `editor_returned_inner`) and then settles once in `settle_and_send` (event_loop.rs:745). For 23 of the 39, the un-suffixed wrapper that calls inner-then-settle is `#[cfg(test)]`: in this slice app.rs has 7 (`connect_failed` 987, `disconnected` 1009, `write_failed` 1060, `write_failed_tracked` 1090, `open` 1506, `load_failed` 1570, `toggle_ledgers` 1692) and app_mouse.rs has 3 (`on_mouse` 23, `on_click` 170, `on_wheel` 333). So every caller must know the sequencing rule "mutate, then settle exactly once per input", and tests go through a different entry than the product does.
prop: Give `App` one entry that owns the sequencing, for example `App::apply(&mut self, input: AppInput, now) -> Effect`, which dispatches to the private handlers and settles once before returning; the event loop's `handle_inner` match (event_loop.rs:1009-1125) becomes the translation from `Input` to that call. The `_inner` suffix and the 23 test-only wrappers then disappear: tests call the same `apply` the loop calls, which is the rubric's "the interface is the test surface". Roughly 70 wrapper lines go in this slice and about 180 crate-wide.

title: The settings view keeps a second per-key table of defaults and controls beside the configuration schema, and branches on key strings in 29 places
reason: NUMERIC_SPECS (settings_view.rs:2686-2807) has 16 entries with their own defaults. `retry.attempts` defaults to "3" there and in config/src/keys.rs:672-675. `numeric_default` is used once, at 1599, as a fallback. About 19 lines compare key strings. The duplicated defaults are real and can go, either by reading the default from the row or by having the schema pass it along. Moving the slider ranges and value lists into the config schema runs against the docs. The ranges and display units are written down as TUI presentation in docs/tui.md, around lines 1182-1200 (the slider table), and `SettingControl` is documented as derived from the type the schema checks, as 'presentation, not a validator'. The config crate's schema is the validator. The safe saving is the defaults and some of the key branching, not the whole 150 lines.
evidence: The configuration schema (crates/config/src/keys.rs) already carries each key's type, default, tab, label and description, and hands the view a `SettingControl` enum (crates/contract/src/settings.rs:68) saying how to edit it. settings_view.rs adds its own table, `NUMERIC_SPECS` (lines 2686-2807, 16 entries), keyed by the dotted key string, giving each a slider range or value list, a display format and a `default`. The defaults repeat the schema's: `retry.attempts` is `Some("3")` in both (settings_view.rs:2731-2740 and config/src/keys.rs:672-675), `retry.initial_delay_ms` is `"2000"` in both, `compaction.tokens` is `"400000"` in both. `numeric_default` (2885) is what stepping uses when a row is unset (1599), so a schema default changed without this table would step from the wrong value. Beyond the table, `grep` finds 29 lines in the file that compare `row.key` or `key` to a literal (`"hub.default"` at 322, 1525, 3132, 3133; `"web_search.backend"` at 1525; `applies` at 317-345 is an if/else chain over key prefixes). The numeric section (formatting, slider stepping, value lists) runs from about line 2580 to 3070, close to 490 lines.
prop: Move what varies per key into the schema row, where a key is added: extend `SettingControl` with `Slider { minimum, maximum, step }`, `NumberList(values)` and `TextList(values)` plus a display-unit enum, and add an `applies` field for when a write takes effect. The view then switches on the control it is handed and holds no key names; `NUMERIC_SPECS`, `numeric_spec`, `number_list`, `text_list`, `number_slider`, `numeric_default` and the `applies` chain go away, and the remaining number formatting becomes a small module of its own (a real split of the 3,160-line file, since it has no access to `Settings` state).

title: `SettingRow.layer` is a `String` that the view parses back into the `Layer` enum six times and compares to "-c" and "default"
reason: configure.rs:77 has `pub layer: String`, documented as default/global/repository/project/-c/union, and `Layer` sits at configure.rs:23. SettingRow is re-exported from lib.rs:126 and built in crates/main. `layer_named` has the 6 call sites listed (1437, 1621, 1647, 1706, 1740, 1798), and `row.layer == "-c"` is at 1039. The three `layer_name` bodies are identical: settings_view.rs:242, tui/src/remote.rs:470 and main/src/configure/remote.rs:195. docs/code-quality.md:146 states the enum rule. The wire encoding in the two remote.rs files would still map the enum to text at the process boundary, which that rule allows.
evidence: `SettingRow` is a public type that crosses from crates/main into crates/tui. Its `layer` field (configure.rs:77) is documented as one of `default`, `global`, `repository`, `project`, `-c`, "or the layers of a union", but typed `String`, while a `Layer` enum with three of those cases sits 50 lines above it (configure.rs:23). settings_view.rs turns the string back into the enum with `layer_named` at 6 call sites (1437, 1621, 1647, 1706, 1740, 1798) and compares it to literals at 1030-1033 (`"default"`), 1039 (`row.layer == "-c"`) and 3151. docs/code-quality.md, "Types", says a closed set of named cases that crosses a crate boundary is an enum, never a `String`. The inverse mapping `layer_name(Layer) -> &'static str` is written three times with identical bodies: settings_view.rs:242, remote.rs:470 and crates/main/src/configure/remote.rs:195.
prop: Type the field as an enum that covers every documented case, for example `enum Origin { Default, File(Layer), Run, Union(Vec<Layer>) }`, built where the row is made in crates/main and decoded once in remote.rs. `layer_named`, `is_run` and the string comparisons disappear, and `Layer::name()` as one method replaces the three copies of `layer_name`.

title: The seven configuration views expose the same five operations with seven different signatures, and share their protocol types out of settings_view.rs
reason: The signatures are as the finding says. edit_key takes `&Edit` and returns nothing in tools, skills and login; takes `&Edit, &Ctx` and returns Act in rules; takes `Edit` by value in settings; and Mcp and Logout have no edit_key at all. The frame signatures differ (tools :370, skills :478, rules :226, mcp :225). There are several dispatch matches over `self.config_views.open` (619, 668, 698, 763, 1116 and more). The proposal does not fit every view. Login and Logout have no `frame`: they draw their own ratatui overlay (`draw(area, buf, targets)` at login_view.rs:368 and logout_view.rs:333), and the frame match returns None for them (config_views.rs:1133-1135). `Open` also holds Credential and Doctor, which take `frame()` with no arguments. One trait with `frame(&Ctx)` covers five of the views, and the overlays stay special cases, so the matches shrink but do not collapse to one.
evidence: `Settings`, `Tools`, `Skills`, `Rules`, `Mcp`, `Login` and `Logout` each implement key, wheel, edit, click and draw. The first two are uniform (`key(&mut self, &Key, &Ctx) -> Act`), but the rest are not: `edit_key` takes `&Edit` and returns nothing in tools/skills/login, takes `&Edit, &Ctx` and returns `Act` in rules (rules_view.rs:148), and takes `Edit` by value in settings (settings_view.rs:1287); `frame` takes `(width, cost)` in tools, `(width, height)` in skills, `(width, wall_ms)` in rules, `(_usage)` in mcp and four arguments in settings, even though `Ctx` (settings_view.rs:286) already carries width, height and usage. As a result app/config_views.rs dispatches by hand in five separate matches over the open view (lines 620, 669, 699, 765 and 1116), each naming all nine variants. The shared protocol types `Act` (what a view asks of the app) and `Ctx` live in the 3,160-line settings_view.rs and are imported from it by 7 other files; `Act` has variants only one view produces (`McpReconnect`, `McpLogin`, `Reviewer`, `Theme`). Likewise the shared click enum `Spot` (swapped.rs:29) has variants only one view draws, so 13 product matches list `Spot::Revoke(_)` just to ignore it.
prop: Move `Act` and `Ctx` to a small module of their own (or into swapped.rs, which already owns the frame the views draw in) and define one interface there: a trait with `key`, `wheel`, `edit`, `click` and `frame(&self, &Ctx)`, implemented by all seven views (the project rule against single-implementation traits does not apply with seven). Put the per-view extras (`cost`, `wall_ms`) in `Ctx`. The five dispatch matches in config_views.rs collapse to one `fn view_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut dyn ConfigView>`, and adding a view becomes one enum variant plus one impl instead of edits to five matches.

title: `/login` and `/logout` each carry their own copy of the grouped-list state and its key, wheel and target logic
reason: `diff -w` of logout_view.rs:114-182 against login_view.rs:656-718 differs only in the Enter arm (deletable plus confirm versus open_target) and a comment. wheel (183-198 against 719-734), target_rows (272-278 against 616-622) and body_len (202-204 against 738-740) diff empty. login_logout_view.rs is 106 lines. That makes about 85 duplicated lines from these functions alone, before the drawing overlap, which I did not check.
evidence: Both views keep `items`, `selected`, `top` and `said` and move through them the same way. `rows_key` is 69 lines in logout_view.rs (114-182) and 63 lines in login_view.rs (656-718); a diff shows they differ in one 8-line Enter arm and a comment. `wheel` (logout 183-198, login 719-734, 16 lines each), `target_rows` (logout 272-278, login 616-622) and `body_len` (logout 202-204, login 738-740) are character-for-character identical. That is about 95 duplicated lines. login_logout_view.rs (106 lines) already exists as the shared module but holds only the `Item` enum, the `build` function and a row-count helper, so the state and behaviour stayed in both callers. The list drawing (logout_view.rs:333-456 and login_view.rs:423-604) also overlaps: a trimmed diff leaves 76 of logout's 124 lines in common.
prop: Deepen login_logout_view.rs into a `GroupedList` type that owns `items`, `selected`, `top`, with `key(&Key, height, width, said) -> Option<usize>` returning the target Enter landed on, `wheel`, `click_row` and the body rows for drawing. Each view keeps only what differs: logout's confirm step and login's panel, host and waiting steps.

title: The home session list tracks exited and archived sessions with two parallel sets of per-project maps and accessors
reason: home.rs:557-575 holds totals/dirty and archived_totals/archived_dirty/archived_open. The paired accessors at 862-899 and 943-970 have identical one-line bodies on the two map sets. In recent.rs, scoped_first and archived_first (217-262) differ only in which accessor and which RecentAsk variant they use, and answer_scoped and answer_archived (301-312 and 366-377) mirror each other. The proposal would work, and recent.rs would shrink as well.
evidence: `Sessions` (home.rs:547) holds `totals` and `dirty` for exited sessions and `archived_totals`, `archived_dirty` and `archived_open` for archived ones, all keyed by a project name held as a plain `String`. The accessors come in pairs with the same bodies: `note_total`/`note_archived_total`, `total_for`/`archived_total_for`, `mark_dirty`/`mark_archived_dirty`, `clear_dirty`/`clear_archived_dirty`, `is_dirty`/`is_archived_dirty` (home.rs:862-899 and 943-970, about 40 lines each side). Each is a one-line map operation, and the doc comment on `mark_dirty` says "the caller marks only while an ask for the project is in flight", so the protocol (ask once, mark dirty if another trigger arrives, send exactly one follow-up when the answer lands) lives in the caller. That caller, app/home/recent.rs (outside this slice), repeats it for both kinds: `scoped_first` and `archived_first` (217-262), `fan_out_scoped` and `fan_out_archived` (about 268-298 and 334-365), `answer_scoped` and `answer_archived` (301-312 and 366-377). There are 19 call sites of the ten accessors.
prop: Introduce one type for "a per-project paged ask", for example `ScopedAsk { total: Option<usize>, dirty: bool }` in a `HashMap<Project, ScopedAsk>`, with methods that own the protocol (`trigger() -> bool` says whether to send, `answered(total) -> bool` says whether to follow up). `Sessions` then holds two instances, `exited` and `archived`, and the paired functions in recent.rs take which one as a parameter. This removes about 40 lines in home.rs and roughly 100 in recent.rs, and a `Project` newtype would satisfy the identifier rule in docs/code-quality.md, "Types".

title: The changed-files view is a bag of 16 free functions; its state and the order to call them in live in the caller
reason: changed_files_view.rs exports 17 `pub(crate)` free functions plus several pub types, and holds no state. session_views.rs:93-95 holds `figures` and `tracking`, and the file references `changed_files_view::` 34 times. The sequence numstat_body, numstat_fully_parsed, parse_numstat, lookup, count_lines is at 1268-1289, and numstat_body appears again at 1312. One caveat: the fold also reads App state (panel_state.changes(), workspace_root(), workspace()), so the struct's methods would need those passed in.
evidence: changed_files_view.rs (900 lines) exports 16 `pub(crate)` functions and no state: `ranked`, `diff_command`, `numstat_command`, `parse_numstat`, `numstat_body`, `numstat_fully_parsed`, `tracking_command`, `parse_tracking`, `count_lines`, `resolve_figures`, `lookup`, `answer`, `first_hunk_line`, `list_rows`, `file_takes`, `row_path`, `frame`. app/session_views.rs holds the view's state (`figures` and `tracking` at lines 93-95) and calls into the module at 30 places. Folding one git answer takes five calls in a fixed order that the caller must know (session_views.rs:1268-1289: `numstat_body`, then `numstat_fully_parsed`, then `parse_numstat`, then `lookup` per path, then `count_lines`), and the same `numstat_body` step is repeated for the tracking answer at 1312-1313. The interface is nearly as large as the implementation, which is the rubric's definition of a shallow module.
prop: Make the module own its state: a `ChangedFiles` struct holding the figures and tracking answers, with `queries(paths) -> [command; 2]`, `numstat_answered(output, exit_code)`, `tracking_answered(output, exit_code)`, `selected_path(at)` and `frame(ctx)`. The parsing functions become private, tests exercise the struct through those five methods, and session_views.rs loses the sequencing knowledge and about 60 lines.

title: Terminal capabilities are nine loose fields on `App` with sixteen one-line setters and getters, and three of them can disagree
reason: The nine fields are at app.rs:308-345 and the setters and getters at 1205-1306. `logo_cell_ok` can be computed: `set_sixel` (1238) sets it only when the measured cell passes `cell_ok`, and `set_measured_cell` (1257) recomputes it only while `sixel` is set, so it always equals `sixel && measured_cell.is_some_and(cell_ok)`. It can be derived instead of stored. Most of the accessors would move into the new struct rather than disappear, since the loop still sets the detection results, so the net lines removed are small, about 20, and the '60 lines' are mostly relocated. My rough grep counted about 65 fields on App, not 69.
evidence: `App` has 69 fields. Nine of them describe what the terminal can do: `kitty`, `graphics`, `iterm`, `sixel`, `measured_cell`, `logo_depth`, `logo_rejected`, `logo_cell_ok` and `cell` (app.rs:311-345). They are served by 16 methods at app.rs:1205-1306, most of them one line (`set_kitty`, `kitty`, `set_graphics`, `set_iterm`, `iterm`, `set_sixel`, `sixel`, `set_measured_cell`, `measured_cell`, `set_logo_depth`, `set_logo_rejected`, `logo_rejected`, `logo_cell_ok`, `set_cell`, and two test-only readers). `sixel`, `measured_cell` and `logo_cell_ok` encode one fact three ways: `set_sixel` (1238) sets both booleans only if the cell is measured and in bounds, and `set_measured_cell` (1257) must remember to recompute `logo_cell_ok` when `sixel` is set. docs/code-quality.md, "Types", asks for an enum where fields can contradict, and "Size" asks that a feature's state be its own struct behind one `App` field, as the other 30-odd features on `App` already are.
prop: Move the nine fields into one `Terminal` (or `Capabilities`) struct in its own file behind a single `App` field, with the logo protocol decided by one method that returns an enum (pixel logo, kitty, iTerm, Sixel) from the detected facts, so `logo_cell_ok` is computed rather than stored. The loop sets detection results on that struct directly, and about 60 lines of pass-through accessors leave app.rs.

title: Nineteen product files in the slice exceed the 800-line threshold; the three largest have seams with state of their own
reason: `wc -l` over non-test files directly in crates/tui/src finds 19 over 800 lines, and docs/code-quality.md:162-166 sets the 800-line threshold. window.rs:337-350 has the four shell fields, with `shells` as an unnamed `(usize, usize, String, bool)` tuple. model_picker.rs:283-292 has awaiting, only_pending and sent, all keyed by the command id string. on_session starts at app.rs:2202. I did not re-count the 27 shell use sites or the outside files' map edits.
evidence: `wc -l` over the non-test files directly in crates/tui/src finds 19 over 800 lines: settings_view.rs 3,160, app.rs 2,976, window.rs 2,745, event_loop.rs 2,145, login_view.rs 1,946, model_picker.rs 1,719, home.rs 1,476, configure_fake.rs 1,223, turn.rs 1,184, remote.rs 1,099, swapped.rs 997, keys.rs 969, offer.rs 940, input.rs 940, changed_files_view.rs 900, format.rs 873, markdown.rs 864, rows.rs 827, view.rs 802. Seams I verified: (1) settings_view.rs: the list-entry page editor (`page_key` through `new_entry`, lines 2003-2190, plus `page_frame` 2485-2578) works on its own `Page` struct, and the number formatting and stepping code (2580-3070, about 490 lines) touches no `Settings` state at all. (2) window.rs: shell command output is four fields of `Pages` (`shells`, `shell_index`, `shell_runs`, `shells_running`, lines 339-349; `shells` is an unnamed tuple `(usize, usize, String, bool)`) used at 27 places, all inside window.rs, by about 255 lines of methods and helpers (1206-1245, 1373-1396, 2061-2180, 2438-2505). (3) app.rs: `on_session` is 611 lines and `on_hub` 260. (4) model_picker.rs: one sent `model` command is tracked in three public maps keyed by the same command id (`awaiting`, `only_pending`, `sent`, lines 279-292), which app/model_picker.rs (304, 478-489, 556-558) and app/reconnect.rs (91-93) insert into and remove from by hand in step.
prop: Split at these seams rather than by line count: `settings_view/number.rs` (pure functions) and `settings_view/page.rs` (owns `Page`); `window/shells.rs` with a `Shells` struct that owns the four fields and a named row struct in place of the tuple; `on_session` into the three session cases as described in the duplicate-block finding; and one `HashMap<CommandId, SentModel>` in the model picker where `SentModel` holds the reference, level and an enum of what acceptance does (write these settings, or mark session-only), with `sent`/`accepted`/`rejected`/`forget` methods so the two outside files stop touching the maps.

title: A command's answer has an owner tag but no single dispatch, so every feature re-matches all 44 owners
reason: Opened outbox.rs:56-163: `Waiting` has 44 variants. `Answer::of` (answer.rs:26) reads the tag once. I found the 11 full matches (each lists `Waiting::OfferImport`): app.rs:1792, 1912, 2233; config_views.rs:1269; session_views.rs:1050, 1136; rewind/send.rs:262, 328; home.rs:912, 1157; panel.rs:1225. `on_session`'s first match (app.rs:2207-2266) acts only on ChangeWorkspace and ClearClose. Outside test files, `outbox.settled(` appears 72 times in 25 files and `outbox.wait(` 60 times in 27, so the reviewer's counts are close. The ordering comments at app.rs:2267-2289 are real: tags are settled early so that the exits further down do not leak them. The proposal overstates what disappears. Not every `settled` call follows an answer. Some run on paths with no answer at all: `write_failed_id`, disconnect and link-lost handling (for example delete/settlement.rs:102-165). Those calls survive `take_answer`. Routing also depends on which link the answer came on and on the attached session, so the one dispatch still needs that context. The roughly 405 lines of no-op arms are real, but they overlap with the savings claimed in #1 and #4.
evidence: When a command is sent, the sender registers which feature waits for its answer as a `Waiting` value (44 variants, outbox.rs:57-162). When the answer arrives, `Answer::of` (answer.rs:26) looks the tag up once, but then the line is offered in turn to `pass_line`, `home_answer`, `on_hub` or `on_session`, `panel_line`, `session_views_line`, `config_views_line` and others, and each one matches the full `Waiting` enum again to find the two or three variants it owns. I counted 11 such full matches (app.rs x3, session_views.rs x2, home.rs x2, rewind/send.rs x2, config_views.rs x1, panel.rs x1) containing about 405 lines of arms that do nothing (`=> {}`, `=> None`, `=> return Vec::new()`). In `on_session` the first match (app.rs:2206-2266, 60 lines) acts on 2 of 44 variants. Removing a tag once its answer is handled is also left to callers: `outbox.settled(` is called 70 times in 24 files and `outbox.wait(` 58 times in 25 files, with comments explaining ordering between handlers (for example app.rs:2267-2289, app.rs:1931-1942). The five functions that do this routing are 1,787 lines: `on_session` 610 (app.rs:2202), `home_answer` 548 (home.rs:722), `on_hub` 256 (app.rs:1723), `session_views_line` 214 (session_views.rs:994), `pass_line` 159 (attach_fold.rs:510).
prop: Make the outbox the deep module for the whole request/answer round trip. `Outbox::take_answer(line)` should remove the tag and return one typed value (owner plus accepted/rejected payload), and `App` should have exactly one `match` on the owner that calls that owner's `answered`/`refused` handler. Each feature then exposes two functions instead of a line filter, the 11 full matches collapse to one, and the 70 scattered `settled` calls disappear because settling is part of taking the answer. Adding a new owner becomes one variant and one arm.

title: Fifteen matches list about 70 ignored event kinds each: 1,059 lines of no-op arms
reason: I re-counted with awk. All 15 anchors start runs of 57 to 75 consecutive `| EventKind::` lines (app.rs 2367/2480/2893 =75, 2736=61; form.rs 75; panel.rs 235=64, 453=57, 572=64, 1287=75; quota.rs 75; config_views.rs 72; credential.rs 75; items.rs 74; output.rs 72; fold.rs 70). They total exactly 1,059 lines. I checked what each match acts on: is_block acts on 2 kinds, panel.rs:453 on 3, items.rs on 2, output.rs on 4, and rewind/fold on about 6. docs/code-quality/lints.md:78-80 says what the reviewer quotes. One caveat: rewind/fold.rs rebuild is a fold over every held line and may deserve to stay exhaustive, which the proposal already allows for. The if-let chains that replace these matches add some lines back, so the net saving is about 800.
evidence: The project forbids a `_` arm on an enum, so a `match envelope.kind()` that cares about two kinds must name every other `EventKind`. In this slice 15 matches end in a run of 57 to 75 consecutive `| EventKind::X` lines whose arm is empty; the runs total 1,059 lines (counted with awk; the anchors are the first line of each run). Most of these matches handle very few kinds: `reply_ack` (form.rs:59) and the two blocks in `on_session` handle only `CommandAccepted` and `CommandRejected`; `panel_branch` (panel.rs:1258) handles three; `is_block` (app.rs:2869) handles two. The project's own lint guide says this is the wrong tool: "A match that handles one variant and ignores the rest uses `if let` or `matches!`; the lints are for matches that must grow with the enum" (docs/code-quality/lints.md:78-80). Every new event kind added to the contract crate currently needs an edit at all 15 sites although none of them will act on it. Related: the payload is decoded separately at each stop with the `read!` macro (62 uses in the slice, 19 of them decoding `CommandAccepted` or `CommandRejected` for the same line), although `contract::events::Event::from_envelope` (crates/contract/src/events.rs:140) already decodes a line once into a typed enum.
prop: For the sites that only want command answers, take the typed answer from the single dispatch proposed in the previous finding instead of matching on kind. For the remaining sites that want two to four kinds, use `if let`/`else if` on the kind as `session_views_line` already does (session_views.rs:1006-1023), or decode once with `Event::from_envelope` and pass each feature only the variants it folds. Keep an exhaustive match only where a fold really must consider every kind (the pages fold).

title: `App` is one type with 721 methods in 50 files; several 'state' structs are field bags with all behaviour on `App`
reason: The `App` struct at app.rs:263-459 has 69 fields. 50 of the 65 non-test files under app/ plus app.rs contain an `impl App` block. A grep of `self.X.` reaches gives: session_views 119 field reaches and 0 method calls, config_views 96 and 0, items 70 and 3, completion 57 and 3. Against that, find has 0 and 108, screen 0 and 127, notices 0 and 68. docs/code-quality.md:179 ('are not a split') and :204 ('its own struct behind one `App` field') say what the reviewer quotes. I did not re-count the 721 methods.
evidence: The `App` struct has 69 fields (app.rs:263-459). 50 of the 65 product files in the slice contain an `impl App` block; those blocks hold 22,360 of the 35,771 lines and define 721 methods (another 86 `App` methods sit in sibling files such as history.rs and app_mouse.rs). Because they are all methods on the same type, every one of them can read and write all 69 fields, so the files are a table of contents, not modules with interfaces. `docs/code-quality.md` ("Size") says exactly this is not a split: "Lines moved into another file that still reach the parent's private state ... are not a split", and asks for "a view's state is its own struct behind one `App` field". Some state does live in its own struct, but for several of them the struct has no behaviour: I counted direct field reaches versus method calls from `impl App` code. `self.session_views.` has about 120 field reaches and 0 method calls; `self.config_views.` 99 and 0; `self.items.` 70 and 3; `self.completion.` 60 and 3. `Home` is touched from 27 files (`self.home.questions` 83 times, `.sessions` 44, `.launch` 33, `.subs` 31). For contrast, `self.find.` has 0 field reaches and 108 method calls, `self.screen.` 0 and 127, `self.notices.` 0 and 68: those are real modules and show the shape the rest could take.
prop: Deepen the field-bag structs one at a time, starting with `SessionViews` and `ConfigViews` (1,465 and 1,509 lines, each confined to one or two files already). Move the logic from `impl App` onto the struct, make its fields private to its file, and give it a small interface: open, key, click, answered, refused, draw. Where a view needs something from the rest of the app (the attached session id, the notices, a way to send a command), pass it in as an argument or return it as a value, as `Find` does. `App` keeps only routing. This does not delete many lines by itself, but it is what makes the files independently testable and stops features colliding on `App`.

title: Outgoing commands are turned into text at once, then recovered by parsing the text; a tracked and an untracked path run side by side
reason: `Sent` (app.rs:164) and both `Effect::Send(Vec<String>)` and `SendTracked(Vec<Sent>)` (app.rs:177-182) exist. `write_failed_inner` (app.rs:1065) recovers ids through `hub_id` and falls back to a JSON parse, and `write_failed_tracked_inner` (app.rs:1098) does the same job with carried ids. Its own doc comment says the typed path exists so that 'a tampered line id cannot mis-settle', which supports unifying on it. `Outbox::wrote` (outbox.rs:405) parses id, session_id and command out of the line text. Outside tests I counted 47 `Effect::Send(` uses, 21 `SendTracked(` uses and about 30 `note_hub_sent`/`fold_line` calls, close to the reviewer's numbers. I did not open the hooks_offer parse. The estimate is somewhat high, because the unified type still needs constructors at every send site.
evidence: A command is built from typed values (`hub_line`, `session_line`, outbox.rs:436 and 451) and immediately becomes a `String`. Later code needs the id, session or arguments back and gets them by parsing JSON: `Outbox::wrote` parses every written line to find `id`, `session_id` and `command` (outbox.rs:405-425); `write_failed_inner` parses unsent lines for `id` (app.rs:1076-1081); `home_unsent` does the same (exit.rs:424-431); the hooks offer parses the kept `start` line back into a `Start` struct (hooks_offer.rs:188-191). To avoid the parsing, a second representation `Sent { id, line }` was added (app.rs:164), which produced parallel paths that do the same job: `Effect::Send(Vec<String>)` (43 uses) beside `Effect::SendTracked(Vec<Sent>)` (17 uses) and `ExitTracked`; `write_failed_inner` beside `write_failed_tracked_inner`; `home_unsent` beside `home_unsent_tracked`. The untracked path is bridged with a side table, `hub_sent`, that pairs an id with its line and is looked up by comparing whole line strings (`hub_id`, outbox.rs:333-338), kept in step by 11 `note_hub_sent` and 15 `fold_line` calls in 7 files. `on_line` still returns `Vec<String>`, so anything sent from a fold must go through that side table.
prop: Have one outgoing type that keeps the id (and session, and whether a reconnect resends it) beside the text, and use it everywhere: `on_line` returns it, `Effect::Send` carries it. Then `Effect::SendTracked`, `write_failed_inner`, `home_unsent`, the `hub_sent` table with `note_hub_sent`/`fold_line`/`hub_id`/`purge_hub`, and the three id-recovering JSON parses can be deleted, and `wrote` reads fields instead of parsing. For the hooks offer, keep the typed `Start` args in the outbox next to the line.

title: `on_session` contains the same 100-line block twice
reason: I extracted app.rs:2343-2442 and 2453-2555 and ran diff. The only difference is a three-line comment ('No `commands_answered` ...') in the second range. Each copy holds the 75-line ignored-kinds list. Extracting one if-let helper would remove close to one whole copy and most of the other. The saving overlaps with #1.
evidence: Inside `on_session` (610 lines, app.rs:2202-2811), the branch for a line from the open delegate's session (app.rs:2343-2442) and the branch for a line from any other non-attached session (app.rs:2453-2555) each contain a `match envelope.kind()` that settles an accepted or rejected command and applies a workspace change. I extracted both ranges and ran `diff`: the only difference is a three-line comment in the second. Each copy is 100 lines, 75 of which are the ignored-kinds list. The attached-session branch repeats the same accepted and rejected steps a third time with extra work around them (app.rs:2590-2600 and 2664-2683).
prop: Extract one function, for example `settle_answer(envelope, move_from, waiting) -> Vec<String>`, that does the accepted/rejected settlement and the workspace-change follow-up, and call it from all three branches; write it with `if let` on the two kinds so it carries no ignored-kinds list. That also shortens `on_session` to the point where its remaining stages (settle tags, route to the delegate, route to features, fold pages) can be read in one screen.

title: `/archive` is a second copy of the `/delete` state machine
reason: The files are 761, 240 and 537 lines. Diffing `delete_command_close` against `archive_command_close`, and the two `*_target_project` functions, shows they differ only in the field name and the word in the notice, as claimed. The reviewer understates the other differences, though. `delete_command_session_left` returns `Vec<Sent>` (the tracked path) where archive's returns `Vec<String>`. Delete works on a confirmed set of sessions (`delete_stopping_sets` returns a target, a list of sessions and a name), while archive works on a single target. Delete also has an extra `Asked` state and its own `validated_sets` and question logic. Sharing one module is reasonable, but it has to be generic over a set versus a single target and over the tracked versus untracked send. The real saving is therefore smaller than 300.
evidence: Both commands run the same sequence: ask the hub which sessions are affected (a dry run), stop the ones still running, wait for each to leave, then send the final command. `/delete` adds a confirmation question in the middle. The code is two parallel sets: delete.rs (761 lines) plus delete/settlement.rs (240) against archive.rs (537). Pairs I compared line by line: `delete_command_close` and `archive_command_close` (about 30 lines each, identical except the field name and the word "deleted"/"archived" in the notice); `delete_command_session_left` and `archive_command_session_left` (identical until the final send); `delete_command_finish` and `archive_command_finish` (44 and 36 lines, the `keep_closing` half identical); three `*_generation` helpers each (26 lines per file, same bodies on different variants); `delete_target_project` and `archive_target_project` (identical bodies); `*_command_disconnected` and `*_command_link_lost` in both. The owner enum mirrors it with six variants, `DeleteDiscovery`/`DeleteStop`/`DeleteFinal` and `ArchiveDiscovery`/`ArchiveStop`/`ArchiveFinal` (outbox.rs:98-116), which every full `Waiting` match then lists in pairs. One shared helper already exists (`command_tag_ids`, delete.rs:608) with a comment that it is there so the two "cannot drift apart".
prop: Write one cascade module with one state enum (`Idle`, `Discovering`, `Asked`, `Stopping`, `Finishing`) parameterised by the operation (delete or archive: the final command to send, whether to ask first, and the notice wording). Collapse the six owner variants to three carrying the operation. The stop, session-left, finish, disconnect and generation logic then exists once.

title: Callers must remember to call `settle` after every input: 26 `_inner` functions, 19 of whose settling wrappers exist only for tests
reason: `settle` exists (history.rs:625), and the pattern of `_inner` plus a `#[cfg(test)]` wrapper is real. My grep found about 39 `_inner` definitions and about 23 test-only wrappers, including connect_failed, disconnected, open, toggle_ledgers, on_press, on_edit, on_drag and write_failed_tracked. event_loop.rs has 43 `_inner(` calls. However, the claim that the loop relies on 'remembering to settle' is overstated. Settling is centralised in `settle_and_send` (event_loop.rs:745, called at 741, 1003 and 1144). The loop also deliberately batches hub lines and settles once at the end of a batch (comment at event_loop.rs:641-647). It sends lines in the middle of an input before that input settles (`send_inner`, line 755), and it puts frames between Bytes inputs. A plain `apply(input) -> Effect` would have to keep the batching, the mid-route sends and the framing. The proposal mentions a batch entry but not the other two.
evidence: After any input, `App::settle` (history.rs:625) must run once to redo layout and trim pages. The app does not enforce this. Instead each input handler exists twice: `X_inner`, documented as "Handles the route without settling; the caller owns the layout pass", and `X`, which calls `X_inner` then `settle`. There are 26 `_inner` functions in the slice. For 19 of them the wrapper `X` is marked `#[cfg(test)]` (for example `connect_failed`, `disconnected`, `open`, `toggle_ledgers`, `on_press`, `on_edit`, `on_models`, `on_files`, `on_image`, `on_feedback`, `on_drag`), so the tests call an entry point the shipped program never uses, and the shipped program (event_loop.rs, 43 calls to `_inner` functions) relies on the loop remembering to settle afterwards. Other inputs (`image_viewed`, `on_install`, `on_login`) have no `_inner` twin and follow the same unwritten rule under a different name. The slice carries 119 `#[cfg(test)]` attributes in product files, 39 of them on functions (about 295 lines), plus a test-only field on `App` written from inside the production `rejected_session` (app.rs:386-390, 2046-2049).
prop: Give `App` one entry point for inputs, `apply(input) -> Effect` (the loop already has an `Input` enum, event_loop.rs:1040-1128), which routes and then settles. A batch of inputs can be a second entry that settles once at the end. The `_inner` suffix, the 19 test-only wrappers and the loop's knowledge of when to settle all go away, and tests exercise the same interface the program uses.

title: Command ids and session ids are plain `String`s in the outbox although newtypes exist; a typed event is read as raw text
reason: Confirmed in the code: `Phase::Pending { command_id: String }` (outbox.rs:26), `Kept.id: String` (186), `waits: Vec<(String, Waiting)>` (215) and `Answer.id: &str` (answer.rs:17). `ImageFetch`/`ImageDisplay` use `session: String` while `Subscribe` uses `SessionId` (outbox.rs:67-87). `is_block` (app.rs:2869-2890) compares raw strings such as "reviewer", "deny" and the three cause names. The typed `Escalation` (action.rs:417) and `DecidedBy` (action.rs:521) enums exist, and docs/code-quality.md:136 requires newtypes. I did not re-count the 58 `id: &str` parameters.
evidence: `docs/code-quality.md` ("Types") requires each kind of identifier to be its own newtype, and `contract::CommandId` and `contract::SessionId` exist. In the outbox the command id is a `String` or `&str` almost everywhere: `Phase::Pending { command_id: String }` (outbox.rs:26), `waits: Vec<(String, Waiting)>` (215), `pending: HashMap<String, (Kind, Draft)>` (221), `Kept.id: String` (186), `Answer.id: &str` (answer.rs:17), and 58 function parameters spelled `id: &str` across 22 files, while the same slice mentions `CommandId` 80 times and converts back and forth with `.0`. Inside one enum the session is typed in some variants and not others: `Waiting::Subscribe { session: SessionId }` beside `Waiting::ImageFetch { session: String }` and `ImageDisplay { session: String }` (outbox.rs:67-76). Separately, `is_block` (app.rs:2869-2890) decides whether the reviewer blocked a call by comparing JSON strings (`decided_by == "reviewer"`, `decision == "deny"`, cause in `"consecutive_blocks" | "session_blocks" | "reviewer_failed"`), although the contract crate has typed `DecidedBy` and `Escalation` enums (crates/contract/src/events/action.rs:521 and 417); the same rule says a JSON name is parsed into its enum where it enters.
prop: Key the outbox by `CommandId` and take `&CommandId` in its interface and in the feature handlers; use `SessionId` in the two image variants. In `is_block`, decode `PermissionResolved`/`PermissionRequested` with the existing typed structs and match on the enums, so a new cause or decider is a compile error here instead of a silent miss.

title: Slash-command table: all 46 handlers return `Some`, 17 are the same one-liner, and aliases live in a second table keyed by name text
reason: The handler type `fn(&mut App, &str) -> Option<Effect>` is at commands.rs:51. `aliases_of` (commands.rs:60-77) is a separate match on the name text with 12 entries, and dispatch at commands.rs:954-957 consults both tables. In the handler range no bare `None` is returned: the `return Effect::None` lines belong to an inner `App` method. The one-liners: 7 are pure `Some(app.open_config_view(...))` (Settings, Tools, Mcp, Skills, Rules, Login, Logout). Doctor is the config-view form plus `draft.clear()`. 8 are `draft.clear()` plus `open_session_view` (Hooks, Rewind, AllDelegates, Context, Usage, Status, ChangedFiles, ReleaseNotes). Jobs has extra logic. That makes about 16 of these functions, not 17, so the line estimate is a little high.
evidence: The command table (commands.rs:80-369, 48 rows) is a good registration seam. Three details are heavier than needed. First, the handler type is `fn(&mut App, &str) -> Option<Effect>` (commands.rs:51), but I checked all 46 `run_*` functions (commands.rs:371-724) and none ever returns `None`; the `Option` is only produced by the table lookup itself (commands.rs:954-957). Second, 17 handlers differ only in one enum value: 8 are exactly `Some(app.open_config_view(ConfigView::X))` and 9 are `app.draft.clear(); Some(app.open_session_view(SessionView::X))`. Third, a command's other names are not a field of its row; they are a separate `match` on the name string (`aliases_of`, commands.rs:60-77, 12 entries), so a renamed row silently loses its aliases and both the list and dispatch must consult two tables.
prop: Change the handler's return type to `Effect`. Let a row say what it runs as a small enum: `OpenConfigView(ConfigView)`, `OpenSessionView(SessionView)` or `Run(fn)`, which deletes the 17 one-line functions. Add an `aliases: &'static [&'static str]` field to `CommandEntry` and delete `aliases_of`.

title: The same operation is hand-applied to 'the shown screen and the stashed screen' at 8 sites
reason: The 'shown plus stashed' pattern does appear at app.rs:896, 1178, 1200, 1342, 1636, 1655 and 1680, at history.rs:650, and at a ninth site the reviewer missed, attach_fold.rs:340. Two claims are wrong. First, `use_renderer` is not the only site that includes the folding overlay: `record_extensions` (app.rs:1674-1688) also updates `Overlay::Folding`, so the 'already drifted' inference is weak. Leaving the overlay out of layout and size changes may be deliberate. Second, the sites do not all apply the same operation: image sizing (app.rs:1330-1347) gives the attached and the shown screens different values. A `for_each_pages_mut` helper fits only some of the sites.
evidence: When a delegate's or job's transcript is opened, the attached session's `Screen` is moved into `self.items.open.stashed` and a new one is shown in `self.screen`. Anything that must reach every live screen therefore has to be written twice, and it is, by hand: session labels (app.rs:896), `set_size_inner` (1178), `set_zone` (1200), the renderer handle (1632), cache invalidation in `use_renderer` (1655, which also remembers the folding overlay as a third), `record_extensions` (1676), image sizing (1342) and `settle` (history.rs:650). Each site repeats `if let Some(open) = self.items.open.as_mut() && let Some(stashed) = open.stashed.as_mut()`. A new per-screen setting that forgets the stashed screen will only show as a bug after a delegate view is closed. Only `use_renderer` includes the folding overlay's pages, which suggests the sites have already drifted.
prop: Let one small type own the set of live screens (shown, stashed, and the folding overlay's pages) and offer `for_each_pages_mut` plus `attached()`/`shown()` accessors (the latter two already exist at items.rs:964 and 986). The eight sites become one call each and the question of which screens exist is answered in one place.

title: Terminal capability detection is 9 loose fields and 14 pass-through methods on `App`, with two flags that can disagree
reason: The nine fields sit at app.rs:309-337. The 14 accessor and setter methods are in app.rs:1206-1305, mixed in with set_flat. `logo_cell_ok` defaults to false (app.rs:502) and is set true by `set_sixel` (1244). `set_measured_cell` updates it only `if self.sixel` (1260). Its only reader checks `self.sixel && self.logo_cell_ok` (home.rs:353), which confirms the two flags are coupled and could be one enum.
evidence: What the terminal can do is stored directly on `App` as `kitty`, `graphics`, `iterm`, `sixel`, `measured_cell`, `logo_depth`, `logo_rejected`, `logo_cell_ok` and `cell` (app.rs:309-340), and exposed through 14 one- to eight-line methods (`set_kitty`, `kitty`, `set_graphics`, `set_iterm`, `iterm`, `set_sixel`, `sixel`, `set_measured_cell`, `measured_cell`, `set_logo_depth`, `set_logo_rejected`, `logo_rejected`, `logo_cell_ok`, `set_cell`; app.rs:1206-1305, about 100 lines). The project's rule is that a feature's state is its own struct behind one `App` field. Two of the booleans depend on each other: `logo_cell_ok` only has meaning while `sixel` is true (`set_sixel` sets both, `set_measured_cell` updates it only `if self.sixel`), so the pair admits the state 'not Sixel, but the Sixel cell check passed', which the 'Types' rule asks to be an enum.
prop: Move the nine fields into one `Terminal` (capabilities) struct with its own methods and hand the drawing code a reference to it, so `App` has one field and no pass-through accessors. Represent Sixel as `enum Sixel { No, Yes { cell_ok: bool } }`.

title: `ConfigViews::default()` names the in-memory fake, which keeps a 1,223-line test double in the shipped build
reason: `ConfigViews::default` uses `Arc::new(Fake::new(Vec::new()))` (config_views.rs:162). `mod configure_fake;` at lib.rs:22 has no cfg gate, and configure_fake.rs is 1,223 lines. Outside tests, the only users are config_views.rs:23; testkit.rs is cfg(test) and commands_testkit is test support. The fake stays in place in a real run: main sets `launch.configure` (main.rs:1292), but `remote::seams` returns neither a seam nor a remote for a Remote launch with no local seam (remote.rs:1081-1087), and event_loop.rs:267-271 then replaces nothing. I could not find the 'bench example' the reviewer mentions. The draw, paging and hover jigs do not name `configure_fake`. They may still rely on the default views working without a seam, so moving to Option plus an 'unavailable' state should be checked against them.
evidence: `ConfigViews` holds the configuration seam as `seam: Arc<dyn Configure>` and its `Default` fills it with `Arc::new(Fake::new(Vec::new()))` (config_views.rs:162); the field's comment says `main` replaces it before the first frame. This is the only reference to `crate::configure_fake` from non-test code in the crate (I grepped the whole `crates/tui/src` tree excluding test files), and because of it `mod configure_fake;` is declared without `#[cfg(test)]` (lib.rs:22), so the 1,223-line fake, with its mutex-guarded canned answers and call recorders, compiles into the release binary. The replacement at start-up is conditional (event_loop.rs:267-271: only when a remote or a seam was supplied), so if neither is supplied the views silently read and write the fake instead of reporting that no configuration is available.
prop: Make the seam a required argument when the app is constructed, or store `Option<Arc<dyn Configure>>` and show the views' existing 'unavailable' shape when it is absent. Then gate `configure_fake` behind `#[cfg(test)]` (the bench example that uses it can include it as test support) so it leaves the release build.

title: Extension input cache keys are 856 lines of hand-written field-by-field hashing
reason: The line ranges are right: turn.rs 438-764, slots.rs 187-409 and chrome.rs 345-650 are almost entirely hand-written hashing. key_of at cache.rs:1250-1269 is the 16-arm match as described. Two details are off. I count about 46 key, hash_key and hash_* functions, not 49, and the chrome range also holds Card::flat() at chrome.rs:615-622, which is not hashing. The bigger error is the claim that only three leaf types lack Hash. contract::events::Outcome (context.rs:555 derives Copy/PartialEq/Eq but not Hash, so hash_outcome at chrome.rs:519 exists), contract::shapes::Usage (hashed field by field in hash_spend), ErrorCode (WorkingLine::key hashes format::code(&retry.code)) and QuotaInfo also lack it. The proposal still works, but it means adding Hash derives across several contract types, plus the float and Value wrappers. evidence: Every renderer input struct (the data an extension slot receives) has a hand-written `key(&self, slot)` or `hash_key` method that hashes each field in turn into a DefaultHasher. title: Test-only accessors and pause points are compiled into product types in five files
reason: The counts roughly hold. title: Tools, search backends and commands each have a Lua adapter and a process adapter, although the Runtime already dispatches both
reason: Opened runtime.rs:273-410. tool_run, tool_run_asking, tool_effects, search_run and queue_command each have a FunctionTarget::Lua arm that matches LuaKind::Tool/Effects/Search/Command. Grep finds LuaKind::Hook constructed only at hooks/chain.rs:159 and LuaKind::Watcher only at hooks.rs:1233. The other four variants appear only in runtime.rs match arms and runtime_tests.rs:442, under the dead_code allowance at refs.rs:77-80. LuaTool (extension_tools.rs:77-166) and ProcessTool (168-250) are near-identical: they differ only in calling self.extension versus self.runtime with a FunctionRef. LuaSearch and ProcessSearch (search.rs:98-128) and CommandRunner::Lua/Process (commands.rs:341-378) follow the same pattern, and hooks.rs:1084-1147 builds the Lua-or-process choice by hand three times. The fix needs care in two places. First, the Lua command path keeps a lazy-start check and its own mapping of rejection codes (commands.rs:337-356), which the unified runner must keep. Second, a FunctionRef holds a Weak reference to the extension where LuaTool holds an Arc, so something else must keep the VM alive; SessionExtensions.lua already does. With those kept, the move is feasible. The fallback (delete the four variants and five arms) would also work. The net saving is nearer 100 lines, because registering the FunctionRefs adds code.
evidence: The Runtime (runtime.rs) is documented in hooks.rs:103-107 as the backend-neutral owner through which every hook, watcher, tool, search and command dispatch resolves. Its tool_run, tool_run_asking, tool_effects, search_run and queue_command each match on FunctionTarget::Lua and FunctionTarget::Process (five functions, runtime.rs:273-410). But product code only ever constructs LuaKind::Hook (hooks/chain.rs:159) and LuaKind::Watcher (hooks.rs:1233); LuaKind::Tool, Effects, Search and Command are constructed nowhere in product code (one test, runtime_tests.rs:442), and refs.rs:77-80 carries a dead_code allowance saying they will be 'constructed as each family wires its dispatch through references'. So the five Lua arms in the Runtime (about 10 lines each) cannot run in a session. Instead Lua goes around the Runtime: LuaTool (impl at extension_tools.rs:77-166, 90 lines) and ProcessTool (168-250, 83 lines) repeat definition(), bound(), effects() and run()/run_asking() with only the call target differing; LuaSearch and ProcessSearch (search.rs:98-128) do the same; CommandRunner::Lua and CommandRunner::Process (commands.rs:341-378) are two match arms building the same AdmittedCall; and hooks.rs builds the Lua-or-process choice by hand three times (metas at 1084-1097, command sources at 1108-1120, search sources at 1135-1147).
prop: Finish the move the Runtime was built for: register each Lua tool, effects function, search backend and command as a FunctionRef at load (as hooks and watchers already are), then keep one Tool adapter, one SearchBackend adapter and one command runner that hold only a Runtime and FunctionRefs. LuaTool, LuaSearch, CommandRunner::Lua, SearchBackendKind and the three hand-written Lua-or-process branches in the loader go away. If that move is not wanted before release, delete the four unused LuaKind variants and the five unreachable Lua arms instead, so the code says what it does.

title: SessionExtensions::load_registry is one 595-line function with ten parameters, building a 14-field record whose Option fields encode three exclusive kinds
reason: load_registry runs from hooks.rs:723 to about 1316 (about 594 lines) and takes 10 parameters; start_process (1380) takes 16. Started (240-257) has 14 fields. It is written out in full at 882, 965, 983 and 1496, mostly with empty fields. The kind is recovered with s.extension.is_some() at 1087 and 1109 and with s.package.is_some() at 1143. start_vm followed by with_browser and an optional with_host_script appears at hooks.rs:856, hooks.rs:1015, start.rs:133 and start.rs:215. The copies differ in small ways: 856 adds without_entry(), 215 applies without_entry conditionally and passes debug None, so the shared method needs a flag for the entry script. The too_many_arguments allowances at 475, 511, 535, 720, 1377 and start.rs:62 exist. A provider-only entry can still carry a VM, so that enum variant needs an Option for it. The split is sound.
evidence: hooks.rs is 2,807 lines, the largest file in the slice and 3.5 times the project's 800-line smell threshold. load_registry runs from line 723 to 1317 (595 lines) and takes 10 parameters; start_process (1380-1530) takes 16. The function does, in order: read installed entries, merge repository candidates, copy seven fields out of the RepositorySet, classify each candidate into provider-only, process or Lua, start VMs, settle names, build commands, choose the search backend, register hooks, tools and watchers, admit processes, and sort. The intermediate record Started (line 240, 14 fields) is written out in full four times (882, 965, 983, 1496; about 16 lines each) with most fields empty, because it stands for three different things: a Lua extension (extension: Some, package: None), a process package (extension: None, package: Some) and a disabled provider-only entry (kept in a separate Vec). Later code recovers the kind with 'if s.extension.is_some() {..} else {s.process_meta()}' (1087-1096) and 'if let (Some(lua), Some(_)) = (&s.extension, &s.lazy)' (1183). docs/code-quality.md, 'Types', asks for an enum where fields describe exclusive states. The same nine-argument start_vm call followed by with_browser and an optional with_host_script appears four times (hooks.rs:856-878, hooks.rs:1015-1036, hooks/start.rs:133-150 and start.rs:215). SessionExtensions itself has 41 fields (62-176) and 61 methods in one impl.
prop: Split the loader at its real seam: a 'classify and start' step that turns one candidate into an enum Started { Lua {..}, Process {..}, ProviderOnly {..} } and a 'fold into session' step with one arm per variant. Put the services every start needs (home, config, clock, locks, state, host script, browser, debug sink) in one LoadContext struct, which removes the too_many_arguments allowances at hooks.rs:475, 511, 535, 720, 1377 and start.rs:62, and give it one start_vm method that also applies the browser and host script. The four Started literals and four start_vm sequences collapse to one each.

title: process.rs keeps a second dispatch path that only tests call, under 13 dead_code allowances
reason: Grep finds no caller outside process.rs and the test files for dispatch_stream, dispatch_stream_with_admission_pause, dispatch_tool, send_request, resolve_family, family_of and Family::. There are 17 call sites of dispatch_stream/dispatch_tool in test files. process.rs has 14 dead_code allowances (148, 319, 342, 407, 442, 511, 541, 711, 723, 784, 801, 815, 852, 885), not 13. The comment at line 37 says the allowance is gone. hang_guard, envelope_line, answer_on and answer_off are used in process/requests.rs, calls/dispatch.rs, oauth.rs and lifecycle.rs, so their allowance reasons are stale. install_process_handler (runtime.rs:172) has no non-test caller. The product path in calls/dispatch.rs:427-530 formats the ran_by strings a second time. The hook state transaction (begin, take_call, discard_call) exists in process.rs only on this test path, so the tests do check something other than the shipped path. One cost: dispatch_stream_with_admission_pause is a timing seam some tests use, and moving those tests needs an equivalent pause on the shipped path.
evidence: ProcessExtension::dispatch_stream (410), dispatch_stream_after_admission (445-505), dispatch_tool (514-538), send_request (544), resolve_family (714), family_of (726-782, seven loops over the registry) and the enum Family (785-794) are named by no product file: grep finds send_request, resolve_family, family_of and Family:: only inside process.rs, and dispatch_stream/dispatch_tool are called 17 times, all in process_tests.rs. Each carries '#[allow(dead_code, reason = "the admission test seam; the session dispatches through its installed runtime handlers")]'; process.rs has 13 dead_code allowances in total. Together this is about 240 lines of a 907-line file. The session's real path is process/calls/dispatch.rs:427-530 (install_handlers and handler_spec), which formats the same 'hook {point}', 'watcher {index}', 'command {name}', 'tool {name}' strings a second time, so the tests exercise a parallel copy of the dispatch rather than the one that ships; the hook state transaction (begin, take_call, discard_call at process.rs:462-484) exists in the test path. Two more of the same kind: Runtime::install_process_handler (runtime.rs:172) is called only from runtime_tests.rs and its allowance says it 'installs the transport's handler in a later part', and the struct comment at process.rs:37 says 'the dead_code allowance is gone' while the allowances remain. Five of the file's allowances (lines 801, 815, 852, 885 on hang_guard, envelope_line, answer_on, answer_off) sit on functions that product code in process/ does call, so their stated reason no longer holds.
prop: Delete dispatch_stream, dispatch_stream_after_admission, dispatch_stream_with_admission_pause, dispatch_tool, send_request, resolve_family, family_of and Family, and move the 17 test call sites to the handlers the session installs (Runtime::hook_with, tool_run and queue_command over the registry's FunctionRefs), so tests cross the same interface the product does. Remove install_process_handler or mark it cfg(test). Then drop every dead_code allowance in process.rs and host/admission.rs and let rustc report what is really unused.

title: The hook chain walk is written seven times with the same skeleton
reason: I read before_tool (before.rs:36-108) and before_compaction (compaction.rs:27-98) side by side. Both repeat the same steps: look up the owner, call hook_with with a decode closure that returns a changed flag, send state lines to pending or to state.queue, return Failed if the hook is blocking or push failed_notice if not, and call set_change_lines at the end. Signatures exist at before.rs:112, before.rs:164, lifecycle.rs:84, lifecycle.rs:150 and hooks.rs:2332. failed_notice is defined three times (before.rs:455, lifecycle.rs:280, compaction.rs:303); the compaction copy hardcodes the point constant but produces the same text. grouped is defined twice (before.rs:29, lifecycle.rs:26). before_compaction returns its notices ungrouped. The grouped doc comment says the loop groups again when it flushes events, so that drift probably has no visible effect. after_tool also has a special case for a path that is not a regular file. Each point returns its own answer type, so the shared runner has to be generic, and the saving is closer to 100 lines than 130.
evidence: Seven functions run a list of registered hooks in order: before_tool (before.rs:36-108, 73 lines), check_tool (112-161, 50), before_message (164-241, 78), after_tool (hooks.rs:2332-2440, 109), before_model_call (lifecycle.rs:84-140, 57), run_additive (150-212, 63) and before_compaction (compaction.rs:27-98, 72): about 500 lines. Each repeats the same steps: skip an entry whose owner_name is gone; (in three of them) return Failed when runs_own_command says so; (in three of them) stop when cancelled after the first entry; call runtime.hook_with with a decode closure that also says whether the hook changed anything; send the hook's state lines either to a pending list or to session.state.queue depending on that flag; on error return a Failed outcome if entry.blocking, else push a notice; and at the end call set_change_lines(pending) if anything changed. The helper failed_notice is defined three times with the same body (before.rs:455, lifecycle.rs:280, compaction.rs:303) and grouped twice (before.rs:29, lifecycle.rs:26). The copies have already drifted: six of the walks return grouped(notices) while before_compaction returns its notices ungrouped (compaction.rs:46, 77, 96), and after_tool does not group either. I could not tell from the code whether that difference is intended.
prop: Add one chain runner in hooks/chain.rs that owns the walk: it takes the entries, the point name, an optional cancel, a closure that builds the argument from the running state, and a closure that decodes and applies one return and says Continue, Changed or Stop(outcome). It owns owner lookup, the own-command check, the state-line routing, the blocking versus non-blocking error rule, the notice and its grouping. Each hook point then keeps only its decode and its fold, and failed_notice and grouped exist once.

title: Eight public ways to load a SessionExtensions, three of them called only by tests
reason: The eight constructors exist at the anchored lines. Call counts match: load_session has 40 call sites, all in tests; reload is called only from tests; load_with_state is called only by load and by test support; the product uses load_session_with_diagnostics (main/src/parts.rs:317) and reload_repository (main/src/reload.rs:687). The claim that all eight only choose defaults is overstated. reload_repository (617-668) carries about 30 lines of its own logic that re-holds the running hook snapshots, and load_session_with_diagnostics sets latest_reason after loading. That logic stays under any options struct, so the saving is smaller than claimed. Merging the load variants into one options-taking load is still sound.
evidence: SessionExtensions exposes load, load_with_diagnostics, load_with_state, load_repository, load_session, load_session_with_diagnostics, reload and reload_repository (hooks.rs:397-668, about 270 lines with their doc comments). All eight only choose which of load_registry's ten arguments are defaulted. Counting call sites across the workspace: load_with_state is called by load and by test_support.rs only; load_session is called 40 times, all in test files (the product calls load_session_with_diagnostics once, main/src/parts.rs:317); reload is called three times, all in tests (the product calls reload_repository once, main/src/reload.rs:687). prop: Replace the eight with one load(LoadOptions) and one reload(&self, ReloadOptions), where the options struct has the five always-present services as fields and seed, repository, start, restart and debug as defaulted fields. title: What a callback 'runs as' is a formatted string that the admission rules parse back with prefix and suffix tests
reason: Confirmed: lua/host_calls.rs:107-119 turns a typed Target into a string, process/calls/dispatch.rs formats the same strings again, and host/admission.rs parses them with strip_prefix, ends_with and starts_with in tool_anchor, model_permitted, delegate_permitted, http_attribution and lock_arg_error. What is overstated: the risk from names. http_attribution uses rsplit_once('.'), so a dot in a provider name does not change the answer, and I found no evidence that names may contain spaces. The proposed enum leaves out the 'harness {name}.{key}' kind that dispatch.rs formats and lock_arg_error checks. The ran_by string is also carried in the request record (process/requests.rs:228, 855), so a Display impl is still needed. Adding the enum and its Display offsets most of the removed lines; the gain is type safety more than line count.
evidence: The Lua side has a typed enum for what a call runs, Target (lua.rs:1063: Command, Provider, Hook, Watcher, Timer, Tool, Search, Effects, Delegate). lua/host_calls.rs:107-115 turns it into a string ('tool {name}', 'command {name}', 'hook {point}', 'watcher {index}', 'provider {name}.{function}', 'search {name}', 'tool {name} effects'), and the process side formats the same strings in process/calls/dispatch.rs:444-520 and again in process.rs:470-523. host/admission.rs then decides permissions by parsing that string: tool_anchor uses strip_prefix("tool ") and !name.contains(' ') to tell a tool's run from its effects (201-217); model_permitted and delegate_permitted use ends_with(" effects") and starts_with("provider "), "watcher ", "search " (224-256); http_attribution uses strip_prefix("provider ") then rsplit_once('.') (291-305); lock_arg_error does the same (338-360). Five functions parse a closed set of seven kinds out of text, and the Lua call sites go typed to string to parsed (host_calls.rs:454, 503, 589). A tool or provider name containing a space or a dot would change the answer. docs/code-quality.md, 'Types', says a closed set of named cases is an enum, never a String. There are also two enums named HttpAttribution, one in host/admission.rs:274 (Provider, Silent, Extension) and one in host.rs:717 (Provider, Extension {extension}), converted by hand in process/context/native.rs:68-78. prop: Make the kind an enum in host/admission.rs, for example RanBy { Tool(name), Effects(name), Command(name), Hook(point), Watcher(index), Provider { name, function }, Search(name), Delegate(job) }, with one Display for the text that goes to logs and the wire. CallbackKind::Request carries the enum; tool_anchor, model_permitted, delegate_permitted, exec_logged and http_attribution become exhaustive matches; the three formatting sites build the enum. Keep one HttpAttribution. Remove the 14 allowances.

title: A process provider is stored inside LuaProvider, with a LuaExtension fabricated only to carry three values
reason: LuaProvider (lua_provider.rs:66-94) holds 'extension: Arc<LuaExtension>' with the comment that for a process provider it supplies only home, directory and clock, plus 'pub(crate) process: Option<ProcessProvider>'. The code branches on that field at lua_provider.rs:281, 709 and 793 and at login.rs:63 and 140. hooks.rs:2249-2268 builds a stand-in LuaExtension::new(name, dir, home, clock), calls LuaProvider::new, uses Arc::get_mut to set the process field, and returns false if get_mut fails. hooks/settle.rs:85-90 builds a never-started LuaExtension per extension only so that SessionCommands::build can settle names, and hooks.rs:1102-1121 builds a second time for real; the comment there explains why the notices are taken from the first build only. The backend enum would remove the patching after construction and the stand-in.
evidence: LuaProvider (lua_provider.rs:66) has a field 'pub(crate) process: Option<ProcessProvider>' and a comment on its 'extension: Arc<LuaExtension>' field saying that for a process provider it 'supplies home, directory and clock only: no Lua provider file is loaded or called'. Five places branch on the field (lua_provider.rs:281, 709, 793; login.rs:63, 140). To create one, SessionExtensions::admit_process builds a LuaExtension with LuaExtension::new(name, dir, home, clock) purely as a metadata holder (hooks.rs:2250-2255), calls LuaProvider::new, then uses Arc::get_mut to reach in and set the pub(crate) field (2259-2267), returning false from the whole admission if get_mut fails. So the type's name says Lua, half its fields (token cache, quotas) apply to both backends, and one field silently changes what 'extension' means. The same stand-in trick appears in hooks/settle.rs:85-90, where a never-started LuaExtension is created for every extension so that SessionCommands::build can be run once for names only, and then run a second time for real at hooks.rs:1121. The session field lua_providers, Providers::lua and Providers::add_lua all hold process providers too.
prop: Give the provider handle an explicit backend: enum Backend { Lua(Arc<LuaExtension>), Process { runtime, runs, owner, home, dir, clock } } constructed by two constructors, so no field is patched after construction and no VM handle is made for a process. The five 'if self.process' branches become one match in a private call method. For settle, let SessionCommands::build take names without a runner (or return the settled names from one build) so the dummy LuaExtension and the second build go away. Renaming LuaProvider is optional and touches other crates; the backend enum is the part that removes the coupling.

title: Five public release and update functions exist only so tests can omit the observer
reason: release.rs:101-110 shows install_docs_if_missing only calling its _observed twin with Observe { debug: None, clock: System }; the others follow the same pattern. title: Package::load_process_provider_with takes a mode and an optional host bundle whose valid combinations are checked at run time
reason: Confirmed: load_process_provider_with (package.rs:323) takes a mode and Option<ProcessProviderHost>. The Session arm returns the run-time error 'a session process start needs its host bundle' (364-369), both arms return a ten-element tuple (351-362), and ProcessProviderHost.session is an Option. The clock is passed both in PackageOptions and in ProcessProviderSession (hooks.rs:1461, 1467). The proposed Sessionless { cli: Option<..> } still covers both callers, so the change works; it is smaller than claimed.
evidence: The function takes (options: PackageOptions, mode: ProcessProviderMode, host: Option<ProcessProviderHost>). For ProcessProviderMode::Session the host must be present, and package.rs:364-369 returns the error 'a session process start needs its host bundle' when it is not; for Sessionless the host is optional and its 'session' field is ignored (the arm passes None at 418-431). title: A second dispatch path in process.rs is reached only by tests, and only that path joins hook state transactions
reason: I opened process.rs:403-552 and 706-795. dispatch_stream, dispatch_stream_after_admission, dispatch_tool, send_request, resolve_family, family_of and Family all carry the 'admission test seam' dead_code allow. grep finds callers only in process_tests.rs (14 dispatch_stream and 4 dispatch_tool sites, plus the cfg(test) dispatch_stream_with_admission_pause).
