title: Two hand-written SSE parsers, one per crate
reason: Both parsers exist as described: provider/src/sse.rs is 53 lines, mcp/src/sse.rs is 126 lines, and both crates depend on net. They differ in more than the three ways listed, which makes merging harder. On an I/O error, provider returns Error::Connection while MCP silently ends (Next::End). On invalid UTF-8, provider fails because read_line is strict, while MCP decodes lossily. In MCP an event line with no data line still opens an event; in provider only data lines count. Provider has no line cap, and adding the 4 MiB MCP cap (pipes.rs:15) would change how a long model stream is handled. A shared reader would need these behaviours chosen or made configurable, so the saving is about 25 lines, not 50, and the change alters error behaviour on one side or the other.
evidence: provider/src/sse.rs (53 lines) and mcp/src/sse.rs (126 lines) each parse text/event-stream line by line: strip CRLF, join data lines with newlines, treat a blank line as the end of an event, and refuse a field named 'database'. They differ in three ways: MCP keeps the event name, caps line length at pipes::MAX_LINE, and returns an iterator-style Next value where provider uses a callback. Both crates already depend on net.
prop: Move one capped, name-keeping event reader into net (or support), and have both crates use it. Provider's callback becomes a short loop over it. About 50 lines go, and the two parsers can no longer drift.

title: Session lookup and project-key resolution is spread over about 15 public functions and six separate walks of projects/
reason: Most of the evidence holds. I opened read.rs:127-275, lib.rs:103-215, name.rs:15-79 and history.rs:33-168. title: escalations/place.rs re-implements the started-session walk and its first-line parse with about 200 lines of hand-written serde visitors
reason: The walk duplication is real. place.rs sessions/sessions_in (27-74) mirrors scan.rs started_sessions/started_sessions_in (39-83) almost line for line, and the first-line read is repeated. But the narrow parse is deliberate. escalations.rs:31-35 and reviewer_shell_calls.rs:48-52 both say the walk goes through place::sessions and never through crate::started_sessions or crate::SessionStarted. The place.rs module doc says only kind, payload.workspace and payload.worktree.repository are read, so no other key is kept. SessionStarted::of clones the raw forked_from and worktree values, which is exactly what this avoids. The proposed `#[serde(default)]` struct with IgnoredAny would not keep the current leniency either. place.rs promises that a payload or worktree that is present but not an object reads as absent and the session is still listed. A derived struct fails on a non-object value and drops the whole line. That is why the visitors exist (place.rs:139-142, 201-205). What can be removed is the duplicated directory walk, about 40-50 lines, by giving the shared walk a callback for the narrow parse. The visitors would stay.

Its sessions/sessions_in functions (lines 27-74) are a line-for-line copy of scan.rs started_sessions/started_sessions_in (lines 39-83): read projects, skip non-directories by file_type, read the first line, sort by id. prop: Give scan.rs one narrow first-line reader. If skipping unread keys matters for speed, use a single `#[serde(default)]` struct with `IgnoredAny` for unknown keys, which needs no hand-written visitors. Have allowed_escalations and reviewer_shell_calls iterate `started_sessions(home)`, adding `repository` and the project key to `Started` if they are missing. That removes place.rs almost entirely.

title: Four separate backward readers of the log's tail, with two identical 64 KiB constants
reason: The tail readers exist as described, and TAIL (read.rs:122) and STEP (scan.rs:356) are both 64 KiB. last_ts, last_line_where and last_line repeat the same open, read-length and return-on-empty preamble. Moving last_kind onto last_line_where would change its behaviour on torn tails. A safe cleanup is to share the preamble and the constant, about 20-30 lines.

title: Log::latest is keyed by kind strings, including made-up keys such as "extension_ui:<ext>:status"
reason: The problem is real. latest(&self, kind: &str) at write.rs:322 looks up a BTreeMap<String, Envelope>. keep_latest builds keys from kind.name(), from the literal "repository_code_offered" (three times) and from the format!("extension_ui:...") keys. I counted 7 production callers: session_status 3, extensions_loaded 2, clients 1, repository_code_offered 1. The private-enum proposal does not work as stated. EventKind derives only Debug, Clone, PartialEq and Eq, not Ord, so it cannot key a BTreeMap without adding Ord to the contract type. kept_seed (write.rs:733-746) also relies on BTreeMap string order to emit the extension_ui keys, interleaved per extension ("<ext>:status" before "<ext>:widget:..."). A derived-Ord enum would put every status before every widget, which changes the seed order. The typed accessors alternative (latest_status, latest_clients, pending_offer) does work.
evidence: `pub fn latest(&self, kind: &str)` looks up a `BTreeMap<String, Envelope>`. keep_latest (write.rs:821-870) builds the keys from `line.kind.name()`, from the literal "repository_code_offered" (used three times at 836-841), and from `format!("extension_ui:{}:status")` / `format!("extension_ui:{}:widget:{}")`. Seven callers in doors, loop and main pass literals: "session_status" (3), "extensions_loaded" (2), "clients" (1) and "repository_code_offered" (1). A typo in a caller compiles and silently returns None. latest_wins (write.rs:764) already lists the closed set as EventKind variants.
prop: Key the map by a small private enum, `Latest { Kind(EventKind), ExtensionStatus(String), ExtensionWidget(String, String) }`, and take `EventKind` in `latest`. Or offer typed accessors (latest_status, latest_clients, pending_offer) so callers never name a kind as text.

title: Registry::open_started and open_extension_started are near-copies, and their caller builds the same JobStarted a third time
reason: open_started (registry.rs:543-599) and open_extension_started (670-727) take the same seven arguments, and both carry #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]. They build the same JobStarted and Unreported{run:1, delegate:true}, push Job::running, and run the latched stop-all. They differ only in tool versus extension, the inbox send (made before the push, under the lock) and the return type. delegate.rs:640-652 builds an identical JobStarted for the extension branch because the registry does not return its own. These are the only two callers. Merging them behind an Owner enum, keeping the extension branch's send-before-push order, works.
evidence: open_started (registry.rs:543-599, 57 lines) and open_extension_started (registry.rs:670-727, 58 lines) each take the same seven arguments, build a JobStarted, build an Unreported{run:1, delegate:true}, push Job::running, compute the latched stop-all and run it. title: The resume path copies DelegateWiring's fields and repeats the fresh-launch sequence

title: Process-group stop sequence is rewritten by every caller because support::group only exports primitives
reason: Opened every anchor. The two loops in tools/src/shell/detached.rs (supervise_restored 359-416 and supervise 471-530) are close copies with the same term_deadline/drain_deadline/take_stop/KILL/park_polled skeleton, so that part holds. They are not line for line the same, though. The restored loop checks liveness through supervisor.group_alive(RestoredLivenessEvent::...) test hooks, uses drain_is_expired, and sends KILL without first checking alive. The child loop checks reaped, and checks alive before KILL. The claim of 'six hand-written stop loops' is too high. mcp/src/server.rs is not a stop loop: it sends TERM in shutdown (578), wait_gone waits up to GRACE for output to end (755-768), and reap sends one KILL (725). It has no DRAIN phase at all. main/src/keeper_child.rs spreads the stop across a stop() function, a timer thread (KILL at GRACE, 782-795) and a reaper loop bounded by GRACE+DRAIN (613-626). extensions/src/host/exec.rs and tools/src/shell/drive.rs weave the stop into their output-drain state machines, with pid mode, hosted stop and seen_empty rules (no signal to a group already seen empty, because its id may have been reused). A single step(now, reaped) machine could merge the two detached.rs loops and maybe exec/drive. It would not take in mcp or keeper_child without changing what they do. Realistic saving is the detached.rs merge plus some shared deadline code, about 40-60 lines, not 150.

It does not export the documented stop sequence: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL once GRACE has passed, then drain for DRAIN while polling every GROUP_POLL. Each caller builds that state machine itself. tools/src/shell/detached.rs has two copies in one file: supervise_restored (359-416) and supervise (471-530), each with its own term_deadline/drain_deadline variables, take_stop handling, KILL escalation and park_polled call, about 55 lines each and nearly line for line the same. prop: Give group a deeper module, for example a `group::Stop` state machine built from (pgid, clock). It owns the TERM, GRACE, KILL and DRAIN deadlines and exposes `step(now, reaped) -> Step { Wait(until), Gone, DrainExpired, Failed(Error) }` plus `next_wake()`. Callers keep only their own reporting. Then GRACE and DRAIN become private, and the two detached.rs loops collapse into one.

evidence: `every_probe_recording_decodes_into_the_actions_and_usage_it_holds` is 113, 94, 124 and 115 lines (446 total). In anthropic.rs, each recording is decoded and then checked three ways. title: 196 test-only disallowed_methods allowances repeat one reason, 'no code under test waits on the clock (ruling ...)', for Manual::advance

evidence: clippy::disallowed_methods appears 342 times, 328 in test code. 196 carry the reason 'no code under test waits on the clock (ruling 6179406086)' and 2 more a variant of it; another 42 say 'fakes-internal advance inside the crates/fakes path exemption' and 37 say 'support::clock self-test deliberately moves the clock' (support/src/clock_tests.rs alone has 37). reason: Opened all three. quota.rs:405-413 really does expect on a config lookup with a default, wait.rs:132 expects after an empty-return check under the same lock (comment at 128-129 explains it), models_dev.rs:309 preserves an abort on spawn failure. title: Capped line reader written three times: mcp pipes, mcp sse, and support::framing
reason: Opened mcp/pipes.rs:126-145, mcp/sse.rs:97-122 and support/framing.rs:1-60. The read_line duplication between pipes and sse is real. But support::framing::read_line_partial strips a trailing CR and reports an over-long line as an InvalidData error that carries the partial bytes, while pipes::read_line does not strip CR, returns Line with partial bytes on an error, and has a distinct TooLong variant. sse treats every error as Eof.
